# Temple Scroll Column 66 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 66:2 — "speak" vs. "declare" vs. "tell" — דבר

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he shall speak to them" | Literal דבר |
| LOGOS | "he shall declare to them" | Formal, prophetic register |
| PNEUMA | "he will tell them" | Plain, accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "declare." Prophetic speech is proclamation, not casual conversation; "declare" captures the authority of the prophetic office. PNEUMA's "tell" is too informal.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 66:3 — "require it of him" vs. "hold him accountable" vs. "hold that person to account"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I myself shall require it of him" | Literal אנכי אדרש |
| LOGOS | "I myself will hold him accountable" | Clear formal English |
| PNEUMA | "I will personally hold that person to account" | Dynamic, emphatic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "I myself will hold him accountable." EMET's "require it of him" is archaic; LOGOS preserves the emphatic divine "I myself" while being clear. PNEUMA's "personally" is too colloquial for divine speech.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 66:9 — "multiply horses" vs. "acquire many horses" vs. "build up a large stable"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "multiply horses for himself" | Literal ירבה סוסים |
| LOGOS | "acquire many horses" | Clear English equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "build up a large stable of horses" | Vivid, interpretive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "acquire many horses." EMET's "multiply" sounds odd with horses in English; PNEUMA's "stable" adds a word not in the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 66:11 — "this instruction" vs. "this law" vs. "this law" — התורה הזאת

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "this instruction" | Project convention for תורה |
| LOGOS | "this law" | Standard scholarly rendering |
| PNEUMA | "this law" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "this instruction." This is the established project convention for תורה (cf. Leviticus conventions). The word means "teaching/instruction" before it means "law."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 66:12 — "fear" vs. "revere" vs. "respect" — ירא

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "fear the LORD his God" | Traditional Deuteronomic formula |
| LOGOS | "revere the LORD his God" | Formal, captures awe |
| PNEUMA | "respect the LORD his God" | Accessible but weak |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "fear the LORD his God." In the Deuteronomic king-law context, the traditional formula should be preserved — the king's relationship to God demands full ירא, not softened "revere" or diminished "respect."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 66:16 — "overtake" vs. "accompany" vs. "chase you down" — השיגוך

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "overtake you" | Literal השיג — to catch up to, overtake |
| LOGOS | "accompany you" | Softer, formal |
| PNEUMA | "chase you down and overtake you" | Dynamic expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "overtake you." The Hebrew image is of blessings pursuing and catching the obedient — "overtake" preserves this. LOGOS's "accompany" loses the pursuit imagery entirely; PNEUMA's "chase down" adds words.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---
